source.title: MaSS: an Accelerated Stochastic Method for Over-parametrized Learning

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some PDF text and table formatting are flattened, but the test-accuracy values can be assigned to the listed architectures, learning rates, and optimizers.
record.tranche_reason: It compares test accuracy for Adam and SGD across image-classification tasks, bearing on the adaptive-optimizer comparison using this study's experimental setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports training-loss and convergence results, but they do not measure the held-out performance named in these claim versions. Cited findings about random-label fitting and optimizer generalization are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly compares Adam with SGD and momentum SGD on CIFAR-10 held-out accuracy. These results bear on V4, although Adam uses its default initial learning rate rather than a documented learning-rate search.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the test-performance conclusion: MaSS has the highest reported accuracy, and larger initial learning rates improve SGD and sometimes MaSS while degrading SGD+Nesterov. The paper's broader conclusion concerns MaSS acceleration and the lack of general acceleration guarantees for ordinary Nesterov SGD.
record.recipe_differences: The study reports test accuracy for Adam and SGD under its image-classification protocol, rather than a dedicated comparison under the version's limited-tuning conditions. The methods use specified initial learning rates; no tuning scope for the Adam comparison is stated.
record.method_sensitivity: The Adam–SGD ordering varies with architecture and SGD initial learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: MaSS improves optimization speed and achieves the highest reported test accuracy among the compared methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A compensated momentum method can improve convergence and held-out performance over the tested optimizer baselines.

record.problems: The test-accuracy results are averages of 3 independent runs, with no error bars or significance tests stated. The Adam comparison uses one initial learning rate per architecture; the text does not describe broader Adam tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No additional held-out-performance results bearing on the listed versions were found. Training-loss curves and synthetic-data convergence experiments do not measure the natural-label held-out behavior in these versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance on the same image task and the role of local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and matched training performance for the reported Adam comparisons.
Held-out performance across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe changes.
Controlled held-out comparisons with and without dropout. Its removal accompanies batch normalization in the test CNN and is not evaluated as an ablation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: SGD+Nesterov test accuracies: CNN 83.06% at 0.01 and 75.79% at 0.3; ResNet-32 92.60% at 0.1 and 91.13% at 0.3. These provide momentum-SGD comparisons with Adam that change the condition-specific verdicts.

At initial learning rate 0.3, SGD+Nesterov diverges in 5/8 CNN runs and 2/5 ResNet-32 runs; its reported accuracies average three converged runs. This selection condition must accompany the missing accuracy rows.
missing.locator: Section 6, Table 1 footnote and following paragraph

record.verdict_notes: All reported test accuracies average three runs; no error bars or significance tests are provided. Adam starts at 0.001, and all methods follow scheduled learning-rate reductions. The results establish condition-specific numerical orderings, not a general optimizer ranking. This study is not an original source for V4.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label generalization.
No network-width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures on the same image task.
The study does not compare broad hyperparameter tuning, weight-decay variants, switching from Adam to SGD, or language benchmarks.
No large-batch test-performance comparison at fixed epoch budgets.
No comparison of test error with and without dropout.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
